activity: Final design: routed boards, serviceable frame, home-built droplet generator. See REPORT.md for what is and is not proven.

hardware.title: Final assembly: nothing overlaps, nothing floats, every screw drawn, nothing collides when taken out
hardware.detail:
1197 solids at real size · 5994 close pairs checked · 0 overlaps
every part fastened to something and connected to the enclosure floor: yes
224 wire conductors, 51.45 m · loose ends 0 · through a solid 0
6 service motions (chuck out, cap off, generator cartridge out, door, lid, one board out): collisions 0
15 printed parts, 378 cm³; each one solid and sound after peeling 0.6-0.8 mm off every surface: yes

pcb.title: Transducer board TB-25: routed; files for JLCPCB
pcb.detail:
4 layers · 342 tracks, 1.26 m · 235 vias · 68 parts placed by the assembler, 21 part numbers from JLCPCB's library
rebuilt from the Gerber and drill files alone: 120 nets, 367 pads · open circuits 0 · shorts 0 · smallest gap between nets 0.135 mm
driver headroom at 18 V: 40.0 % · microcontroller pins 30/30
no board has been built and there is no firmware yet

sourcing.title: Can every part be bought?

land_smooth.title: Landings on a smooth 20 mm part (all directions, imperfect machine)
land_smooth.detail:
0.3 mm droplets: landed 42/42 · median 104 µm · 9 in 10 within 250 µm · worst 333 µm
bare pin tip (first droplets): landed 6/6 · median 185 µm · 9 in 10 within 253 µm · worst 305 µm

land_benchy.title: Landings on the real Benchy geometry mid-print
land_benchy.detail:
under-side sites, 10 % printed: landed 4/6 · median 372 µm · 9 in 10 within 504 µm · worst 558 µm
under-side sites, 45 % printed: landed 12/12 · median 159 µm · 9 in 10 within 384 µm · worst 488 µm
side wall, 25 % printed: landed 12/12 · median 358 µm · 9 in 10 within 1326 µm · worst 2025 µm
this is the weak spot: on thin or crowded geometry some droplets are lost or land in the wrong place

land_fine.title: 0.2 mm droplets (used for the fine shell)
land_fine.detail:
smooth part + Benchy under-side: landed 36/36 · median 76 µm · 9 in 10 within 208 µm · worst 230 µm
Benchy side wall: landed 10/12 · median 269 µm · 9 in 10 within 1204 µm · worst 2058 µm

land_power.title: How much acoustic power is really needed? (cheaper, weaker transducers)
land_power.detail:
71 % of the simulated sound pressure: landed 18/18 · median 80 µm · 9 in 10 within 216 µm · worst 249 µm
50 % of the simulated sound pressure: landed 18/18 · median 65 µm · 9 in 10 within 127 µm · worst 200 µm
40 % of the simulated sound pressure: landed 12/12 · median 106 µm · 9 in 10 within 168 µm · worst 199 µm
the cheapest transducers at their guaranteed minimum reach about 47 % at 27 V, the most the chosen supply gives

land_mu.title: Thicker resin (80 mPa·s, the thinnest hobby resin found)
land_mu.detail: under-side site: landed 6/6 · median 121 µm · 9 in 10 within 160 µm · worst 162 µm

print.title: Benchy at 40 % scale (24 mm long), printed hanging from the pin
print.detail:
0.3 mm droplets, smooth-part landing scatter: 73,533 droplets · surface error 62 µm mean (57 on faces, 111 on edges) · internal voids 1.2 % · built 98.9 % of sites
0.3 mm core + 0.2 mm shell, smooth-part landing scatter: 126,006 droplets · surface error 51 µm mean (47 on faces, 87 on edges) · internal voids 1.5 % · built 99.4 % of sites
0.3 mm, landing errors and losses taken from the Benchy flight tests: 72,463 droplets · surface error 86 µm mean (82 on faces, 127 on edges) · internal voids 4.5 % · built 97.5 % of sites
floor set by droplet size alone on edges: 94 µm for 0.3 mm droplets, 78 µm for 0.2 mm

structure.title: Does the half-built part need structural support?
structure.detail:
own weight, 17 snapshots: stress up to 0.06 MPa, sag up to 11 µm at a resin modulus of 1 GPa
sound field during a delivery, 3 Benchy sites: net force on the part up to 2.2 mN, stress up to 0.17 MPa, movement up to 28 µm at 1 GPa
strength is no issue (resin about 30 MPa); soft, freshly cured thin walls can move by tens of µm, which the print simulation does not include
on the thin side wall 2730 of 8275 boundary-element panels had to be clipped: the solver is at its limit there

twin.title: Digital twin: measure the built machine, correct the model, re-plan
twin.detail:
uncalibrated cheap transducers (14° phase and 15 % amplitude scatter, air 1.5 K off, steady draught): landed 4/4, median 81 µm
board microphones recover the sound speed to 0.02 m/s and the phase error from 13.4° to 0.2° rms; landing after calibration 4/4, 86 µm
camera trap test infers the draught (0.30 m/s vs 0.20 true); with feed-forward 4/4, 94 µm
on this easy site calibration fixes the model but does not change the landing error measurably

uv.title: UV flash from the eleven 405 nm emitters as placed
uv.detail:
0.24 W/cm² typical on any surface orientation (worst 0.10)
typical hobby resin: shape frozen after 17 ms of light; cured through after 46 ms in total (later flashes add up)

geometry.title: Why a polyhedron and not a box, a sphere or flexible boards
geometry.detail:
box 864 transducers: 64 % of a sphere's output reaches the centre · polyhedron 450: 90 % · ideal sphere 450: 100 % (+16 % trap stiffness)
landings still succeed at 40 % of the sound pressure, so the last 16 % does not justify flexible boards and hand wiring

verdict: Simulation supports building a bench prototype; it is not a guarantee. 42/42 droplets landed on a smooth part, 28/30 on real Benchy geometry with some landings off by more than 1 mm. The droplet generator must be built and proven first. See REPORT.md.
